contents.support: An independent symmetric-hyperbolic treatment states a bootstrap-continuation implication for its maximal solution. The current item gives a complete first-threshold proof under its own abstract hypotheses.

source_review.read_extent: Read §3.4 in full, including maximal-interval definition, blow-up alternatives, Lemma 3.10 and Lemma 3.11, PDF p. 26.
source_review.supports: The continuation route and strict-improvement pattern.
source_review.limitations: The source uses its own Sobolev bounds and local-existence theorem; its short lemma is not substituted for the local proof or for an Einstein estimate.

contents.support: A separate semilinear Maxwell–Bloch model illustrates additional conserved quantities and derivative estimates.
contents.reason: It has a different equation and structural hypotheses; no Maxwell–Bloch conclusion is asserted or used in this GR batch.

sources.locator: Complete author-hosted 262-page PDF retrieved. Inspected §6.3, Theorem 22 proof and the continuity/continuation argument, PDF pp. 174–186.

contents.name: §6.3, local existence, maximal time and continuity setup for Theorem 22
contents.support: The proof starts from positive local existence and a continuation criterion, then seeks a strict bootstrap improvement.

source_review.read_extent: Read the setup and initial continuity argument, PDF pp. 174–177.
source_review.supports: How an a priori improvement and continuation criterion combine in a model-specific proof.
source_review.limitations: The conclusion is for a 3D Minkowski null-condition wave system; no GR result is imported.

contents.name: §6.3, Step 1 and Gronwall bound for the nonlinear wave energy
contents.support: The source derives a polynomial-in-time upper bound from a logarithmic weight and then needs a second decay estimate for strict closure.

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete Step 1 calculation, PDF pp. 177–181.
source_review.supports: The borderline weight and polynomial-growth limitation illustrated by the local scalar example.
source_review.limitations: The source’s PDE estimates and exponent differ from the current scalar model; only the method and boundary distinction are used.

contents.name: §6.3, Step 2: strict improvement and closure under a smallness condition
contents.support: The source obtains a strict bootstrap improvement only after additional integrable decay and a small-data condition.

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete Step 2 argument through completion of Theorem 22, PDF pp. 182–186.
source_review.supports: Why an integrable weight can help close a bootstrap when the resulting bound is sufficiently small.
source_review.limitations: Its null-form, dispersive and small-data hypotheses are not present in the abstract contract; the local scalar argument is proved separately.
